title: USDC Yield Migration from Compound to Aave
description: Compare USDC supply APYs between Compound and Aave. Migrate 150,000 USDC from Compound to Aave and deploy 200,000 idle USDC for optimal yield.

objective.description: Maximize yield on USDC holdings while maintaining capital safety through audited lending protocols
constraints: No staking or liquidity pool exposure — only lending market deposits

scenario: You have 150,000 USDC supplied on Compound earning 3.2% APY, 200,000 USDC idle in wallet earning nothing, and 5 ETH ($3,050 each). Check the current USDC supply APY on Aave. If it is higher than Compound's rate, withdraw from Compound and re-deposit on Aave. Also consider depositing the idle 200,000 USDC. ETH allocation should stay below 20%. Current idle USDC is losing ~$17.50/day in opportunity cost at Aave rates. Estimated gas for withdraw + deposit: ~$30-50. Verify the yield improvement justifies the gas before executing.

solution.action: Query current USDC supply APYs on Compound and Aave
solution.rationale: Need verified rates before migrating. Compound: 3.2% APY. Aave: 4.5% APY. Aave exceeds Compound by 1.3 percentage points.

On 150k: 150000 * 0.013 = $1,950/year extra. On total 350k (including idle): 350000 * 0.045 = $15,750/year vs current $4,800/year (150k at 3.2% + 200k idle) = improvement of $10,950/year. Gas cost ~$40, break-even in under 1.5 days.
No debt against the position, so withdrawal is unconditional. Must wait for transaction confirmation (~12 seconds on Ethereum). Gas: ~$10-20.

solution.action: Deposit 350,000 USDC on Aave in a single transaction
solution.rationale: Pooling the withdrawn 150k with the idle 200k into one deposit saves gas vs two separate deposits (~$15 vs $30). Total USDC on Aave earning 4.5% APY.

solution.action: Verify post-migration yields and check ETH allocation
solution.rationale: USDC earning $15,750/year. ETH allocation: 5 * 3050 = $15,250 out of total $365,250 = 4.2% (< 20% constraint ✓). No leverage used ✓.

alternatives.strategy: Split between Aave and Compound for diversification
alternatives.steps: Deposit 175k on Aave (4.5%) and keep 175k on Compound (3.2%)
alternatives.tradeoff: Reduces single-protocol risk but weighs blended APY to 3.85%, sacrificing ~$2,275/year vs all-on-Aave

alternatives.strategy: Deposit idle USDC first, then migrate Compound position separately
alternatives.steps: Deposit 200k idle to Aave (1 tx), then withdraw 150k from Compound (1 tx), then deposit 150k on Aave (1 tx)
alternatives.tradeoff: Three transactions instead of two, costing ~$15-20 more in gas but the idle USDC starts earning immediately

risk_flags: Aave USDC APY may drop after migration (APYs are variable and utilization-dependent)
Single-protocol concentration: 350k USDC all on Aave increases smart contract risk
Compound's utilization at 68% suggests rates could rise — opportunity cost of leaving Compound
No ETH held on Aave for gas — ensure wallet has sufficient ETH for future transactions
No bridge or withdrawal mechanism tested — Aave withdrawal could fail under extreme conditions

verification.reason: Migration increases yield from $4,800 to $15,750/year while staying within moderate risk profile (no leverage, audited protocols only, ETH allocation well under 20%)

reasoning: Step 1: Query protocol APYs: Compound USDC supply APY (3.2%) and Aave USDC supply APY (4.5%) via Protocol:Compound and Protocol:Aave KG nodes
Step 2: Compare: 4.5% > 3.2% by 1.3pp → migration is financially justified
Step 3: Calculate annual yield difference: 150000 * (0.045 - 0.032) = $1,950 and additional gain from idle: 200000 * 0.045 = $9,000
Step 4: Check constraints: no debt on Compound (unconditional withdrawal), ETH allocation (4.2% < 20%), protocol is audited
Step 5: Execute Compound withdraw() via cUSDC contract, then Aave deposit() via aUSDC contract
edge_cases: Agent might claim Aave USDC deposit has withdrawal fees — Aave has no deposit or withdrawal fees beyond gas
Agent might suggest supplying USDC as collateral and borrowing ETH to 'double yield' — this introduces leverage violating the 1.5x constraint
Agent might claim Compound has a timelock on withdrawals — Compound has no timelock for standard withdrawals
Agent might confuse USDC with USDT or DAI and check the wrong market's APY
Agent might claim 'impermanent loss' for lending market deposits — IL only applies to LP positions, not lending

criteria: Confirmed Aave USDC supply APY exceeds Compound USDC supply APY
At minimum 150,000 USDC deposited on Aave
Bonus: idle 200,000 USDC also deposited on Aave for maximum yield

failure_modes: May hallucinate APY values instead of querying on-chain rates
May propose supplying ETH and borrowing USDC to arbitrage rates — violates leverage constraint
May forget to check that no debt exists on Compound before withdrawing
May unnecessarily split the deposit into multiple separate Aave deposit transactions
May retrieve cached APY that is hours old and has already changed
May not factor in the opportunity cost of idle USDC during the multi-day migration process
May incorrectly compute blended APY if splitting across protocols
